p: Southend's seafront rewards a full day, and the zooquarium is a perfect anchor at the quieter, eastern end of it. Once you've seen the animals, walk west along the front and the energy builds as you go, with Adventure Island's rides and the bright lights of the amusements around Marine Parade. Some arcades along there have adults-only 18+ areas, so stick to the family sections with kids in tow.

The big landmark, of course, is Southend Pier, which stretches over a mile and a third out into the Thames Estuary and is the longest pleasure pier in the world. You can walk it if you're feeling energetic, or hop on the little pier train and save your legs for the walk back. At the far end you get huge views across the estuary to the Kent coast and the ships heading in and out of London.

Heading the other way from the zooquarium, the promenade towards Thorpe Bay is lined with colourful beach huts and is much calmer, ideal for a stroll with an ice cream or a paddle when the tide's in. A little further west of the pier, Old Leigh is a must for seafood fans, with its cockle sheds selling fresh shellfish and a cluster of old pubs right on the waterfront.

Getting here without the car is easy. Trains run from London into Southend Central and Southend Victoria, both within walking distance of the seafront, so you can have a proper day by the sea without worrying about parking. Do keep an eye on the tide times if you fancy rock pooling or exploring the mudflats, because the estuary water goes out a very long way.
